commit.message:
Add "Zl" and "Zp" to the characters blacklist

The "Zl" (line separator) and "Zp" (paragraph separator) are also
included in the blacklisted characters.

We introduce a dedicated section in Bolt 1 that we reference instead
of copy-pasting the requirements in several places.

Thanks @vincenzopalazzo for the suggestion and test vectors.

Ban unicode control characters from Bolt12 types

And require that features are minimally-encoded.

Ban unicode control characters from Bolt11 invoices

Note that we already require that features are minimally-encoded.

Add test vectors with invalid utf8 characters

Those test vectors contain a valid signature.
Only the alias is invalid.

Ban unicode control characters from utf8 fields

As discussed in #1260, we should ban NULL and other control characters
in utf8 fields, along with characters that don't provide any value in
node aliases: there's no valid use-case for them.

Unfortunately, unicode cannot provide static lists of characters in each
category, since it is open to extension. We thus more strongly restrict
writers, and set reader restrictions that are more stable.

We also make sure that feature bits MUST be minimally-encoded everywhere
instead of being lenient for `node_announcement` for no good reason.

commit.message:
bolt11: give each invalid vector a single defect

The unknown fields example broke several rules at once (duplicate `p`,
`h`, `s` and `n` fields, each with a bad length), so a reader could
reject it for any one of them and still pass. It was also the only vector
exercising an unknown field type and an `f` field with an unknown
version, so marking it invalid left nothing positive covering either.

Split it in two. The valid "fields which must be ignored" example is back,
carrying just the unknown `2` field and the version 19 `f` field. A new
invalid vector carries a single `n` field of the wrong length, which a
reader that skips the field would accept. We also add vectors for a
missing `p` field and for two distinct `s` fields, so each part of the
exactly-one rule has a vector that only that rule rejects.

The new invoices are signed with the same key and RFC6979 nonces as the
other examples.

bolt11: keep invoice strings next to their breakdowns

Moving the invoices into the JSON file while leaving their breakdowns in
the markdown made the examples hard to follow, as each breakdown no longer
had the string it breaks down. Put every invoice back under its heading,
including the upper case and invalid examples, and generate the JSON from
the markdown so the two can't drift. The JSON descriptions now match the
markdown headings, and the two duplicate `p` vectors get markdown entries
of their own.

The unknown fields example is now invalid, so it moves to the invalid
section with its breakdown.

bolt11: require exactly one p and one s field

The writer section already requires exactly one `p` and exactly one `s`
field, but the reader rule only rejected a second `p`. Nothing rejected an
invoice with no `p` at all, and a repeated `s` was left to each
implementation, which reintroduces the same first-vs-last split for the
payment secret.

commit.message:
bolt-simple-taproot: relax the SIGHASH_SINGLE index rule

The previous wording required any extra input to sit at an index beyond
the last HTLC output. SIGHASH_SINGLE only pairs each signed input with the
output at the same index, so a fee bumping input placed first, matched by
a change output at index 0, is equally valid. State the actual constraint
and leave the remaining indices free.

Fix more broken intra-spec anchors

GitHub keeps underscores from code spans in heading anchors, so
"Definition of `channel_id`" is #definition-of-channel_id, not
#definition-of-channel-id. Fix those, and links to sections that were
renamed:

- BOLT 1: #definition-of-channel_id, #definition-of-short_channel_id
- BOLT 2: "Calculating Fees for Collaborative Transactions",
  "Penalty Transactions Weight Calculation", "Transaction Output
  Ordering", and the dual-funded test vectors, which are now Appendix G
- BOLT 5: the three Expected Weight anchors (to_local, offered_htlc,
  accepted_htlc), and "The `error` and `warning` Messages"
- BOLT 7: drop the TOC entry for a References section that doesn't exist
- BOLT 11: payment_secret/payment_metadata now point to "`payload`
  format"

commit.message:
bolt11: move all invoice vectors to JSON

In this commit, we move every encoded BOLT 11 invoice into the machine-readable test vector file. The prose keeps the detailed breakdowns, while the JSON file becomes the single source for both valid and invalid invoice strings.

bolt11: move invoice vectors to JSON

In this commit, we move the duplicate payment hash invoice vectors into a machine-readable JSON file. The BOLT 11 document now links to the canonical vectors instead of embedding a second copy.

bolt11: add duplicate payment hash vectors

In this commit, we add two signed invalid invoices with two valid-length p fields. One uses distinct hashes to catch first- or last-field selection, while the other repeats the same hash to ensure implementations count fields instead of deduplicating values.

Both vectors use the spec's documented key and have valid signatures and checksums, leaving the duplicate p fields as the intended rejection condition.

bolt11: reject duplicate payment hashes

In this commit, we require readers to fail a payment when an invoice contains more than one p field. The prior payer rule selected the first field, which allowed two components to interpret the same signed invoice using different payment hashes.

A valid invoice now has one unambiguous p field, and the payer must use it.
